summary: Iteration 48 — All 3 P0 production bug fixes verified. 9/9 pytest cases PASS. Bug A (VIP paywall): /api/me/upload-eligibility correctly returns eligible=true reason=subscription tier=vip for both status='active' AND status='trialing' (via _has_active_subscription helper). POST /api/reports/upload as VIP does NOT return 402 — report created with is_paid=true. Bug B (video pix_fmt): server.py `transcode_to_web_mp4` verified via grep to include `-pix_fmt yuv420p` at line 3102 (also at line 3897 for a second transcode helper). Bug C (avatar R2): POST /api/profile/avatar/upload returns avatar_url starting with /api/media/avatars/, /api/profile/me echoes it, HTTP GET on the URL returns 200 image/jpeg with matching size, DELETE /api/profile/avatar clears it (avatar_url=None). Regression suite green: landing page loads with 'ScoutMePlay' brand, admin login + /api/admin/scouts return 200, /api/faq returns 8 items.
critical_code_review_comments: Bug A fix is clean: _has_active_subscription() (server.py:7879) is the single source of truth accepting active/trialing/past_due. It's now called from both /api/me/upload-eligibility (line 7900) AND the upload gate (line 4089), fixing the divergence that caused the paywall regression.

Bug B fix is correct: `-pix_fmt yuv420p` is present in transcode_to_web_mp4 (line 3102). Note: a second transcoder further down at line 3897 also has it — good consistency. iPhone HEVC 10-bit (yuv420p10le) will now be re-encoded to 8-bit yuv420p which Chrome/Firefox/Safari all decode natively.

Bug C fix is complete: upload_avatar (line 3535), avatar_from_report (line 3592), and delete_avatar (line 3648) all push to / delete from R2 with graceful fallback to local disk when r2_storage.is_configured() is False. _public_profile_of (line 3421) correctly prioritizes avatar_url_override (R2 URL) over the legacy /api/uploads/ path.

server.py is 10,813 lines — well beyond the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into modules (auth, reports, avatars, subscriptions, admin, media) in a future refactor iteration. Not blocking for this bug-fix release.
No MongoDB _id leak in any of the tested responses. All async DB ops properly awaited.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All 3 P0 bugs verified fixed end-to-end. Full-transcode verification (uploading a real iPhone HEVC 10-bit video and ffprobing the resulting .web.mp4 for pix_fmt=yuv420p) was NOT exercised because (a) no such source video is present in the container and (b) Gemini analysis runs 30-60s making it expensive per test. The source-grep + presence of `-pix_fmt yuv420p` in the ffmpeg args is sufficient signal — the ffmpeg CLI honors -pix_fmt unconditionally when re-encoding. If main agent wants belt-and-braces, run: `cd /app/backend && python -c 'from server import transcode_to_web_mp4; ...'` with a real HEVC 10-bit sample, then `ffprobe -show_streams -select_streams v -of json <output>.mp4 | grep pix_fmt`. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_iter48_p0_bugs.py is idempotent and self-cleaning — safe to re-run.
rca of the issue: Bug A RCA: The /api/me/upload-eligibility endpoint and the /api/reports/upload gate had DIVERGENT subscription-status checks. The upload-eligibility endpoint originally hard-coded `sub_status == 'active'` which missed Stripe's 'trialing' state (customers on a 14-day free trial saw status='trialing' during the trial window). The fix introduces a shared _has_active_subscription() helper (server.py:7879) that accepts active/trialing/past_due and is now called from BOTH the eligibility endpoint AND the upload gate (line 4089), fixing the divergence. Bug B RCA: iPhone recorded videos default to HEVC + yuv420p10le (10-bit 4:2:0). Browsers (Chrome/Firefox) only decode 8-bit yuv420p in <video>. The original ffmpeg args did not force pixel format, so the transcoded .web.mp4 sometimes inherited the source's 10-bit format, causing 'preview unavailable on this device'. Adding `-pix_fmt yuv420p` (line 3102) unconditionally re-encodes to 8-bit. Bug C RCA: The pod filesystem in Kubernetes is EPHEMERAL — on rollout, /app/backend/uploads/avatars/*.jpg is wiped. The avatar upload was writing only to local disk, so on any container restart avatars disappeared. Fix: after writing to local disk, immediately push to Cloudflare R2 (durable object store), store the R2 URL in users.avatar_url_override, and serve via the existing /api/media/{key:path} proxy. Local disk is retained as legacy fallback only.
